playbook.plays.intro: Short cards the agent follows in specific selling situations. All 13 work from day one. Add your facts to make them specific, or write your own card for a situation.
playbook.plays.suggested_card: A suggested card from your sources
playbook.plays.core_rules: The core rules (stages, one question per message, no early price, credibility rules) are the same for every seller and are not edited here.
playbook.play.line.need: Start with how they handle it today, then ask only what decides the set. Stop at {max} questions.
playbook.play.line.fit: Recommend the smallest set that solves the need and say why it fits.
playbook.play.line.value: One benefit per message, tied to what the buyer said, as a concrete outcome.
playbook.play.line.price_early: Answer with a number or range, say what it depends on, ask the deciding question.
playbook.play.line.too_expensive: Ask what they compare it to, set the price against the cost of the problem, offer a smaller start.
playbook.play.line.existing_solution: Credit what they have. Name the one gap it leaves. Never criticise it.
playbook.play.line.competitor: One factual difference that matters for this buyer. No claims about the competitor.
playbook.play.line.proof: One specific proof: a fact, a customer example or a guarantee.
playbook.play.line.need_to_think: Ask what is still open, answer it, offer a summary to forward and agree when to talk.
playbook.play.line.send_info: Send the one most relevant item, then ask one question that keeps the chat going.
playbook.play.line.not_now: Accept it. Ask when is better and what would make it relevant. No pushing.
playbook.play.line.right_size: Say honestly what is enough. Recommending less when less fits builds trust.
playbook.play.line.handoff: Stop selling and hand off to a person.
playbook.play.saved: Saved to the draft. It goes live with the next published agent version.
playbook.play.restored: Default card restored. Your facts stay.

lead.stage.recommend.wait: Waiting for {name} to confirm the recommended set.
lead.stage.recommend.next: When they agree, the agent sends the quote with the close. If it doesn't fit, it asks why and recommends once more, then offers a meeting.
lead.stage.quote.wait: The agent is sending the quote with the close.
lead.stage.quote.next: It offers to send the order form now, with the delivery estimate.
lead.stage.quote.approval_wait: The quote is waiting for your approval.
lead.stage.quote.approval_next: The agent told {name} it is checking the price with the team. Approve it in Orders, and the quote goes out with the close.
lead.stage.order_form.wait: The quote is with {name}. Waiting for their yes to the close.
lead.stage.order_form.back_wait: {name} changed the need after the quote, and a new version is with them.
lead.stage.order_form.next: When they agree, the agent sends the order form link at once.
lead.stage.after.next: The agent answers questions and confirms here when the order goes through.
lead.stage.after.signed_wait: {name} signed the order form. Waiting for the payment.
lead.stage.after.signed_next: The agent checks the payment when they say they paid.
lead.stage.after.paid_next: The agent answers questions and does not sell more.
lead.stage.after.closed_next: The agent sends nothing more in it.
lead.stage.objection.next: The agent handles it with a play, checks it settled it, then returns to the same point.
lead.stage.human.wait: A person from your team is handling the chat.
lead.stage.human.next: The stage is frozen until the agent is handed back.
buyer.app.offer: The team can offer {n}. Here is your updated quote.
buyer.app.close: If this looks right, I'll send the order form now. Sounds good?
buyer.app.close_by: If this looks right, I'll send the order form now and it can be with you {by}. Sounds good?
buyer.delivery.later_date: Need a later date? Write to us in the chat.
buyer.opener.intro.female: Hi {name}, this is {agent}, the automated assistant of {company}.
buyer.opener.intro.male: Hi {name}, this is {agent}, the automated assistant of {company}.
buyer.sim.opener.female: Hi {name}, this is {agent}, the automated assistant of {company}. You asked to hear from us. What made you get in touch today?
buyer.sim.opener.male: Hi {name}, this is {agent}, the automated assistant of {company}. You asked to hear from us. What made you get in touch today?
playbook.stage.before_quote_help: The quote cannot be made without it. Asked once, once more before the quote, then quoted on a stated assumption.
playbook.stage.optional_help: Makes the recommendation stronger. Asked once, without insisting: if the buyer skips it, the agent moves on and doesn't ask again in the next messages. It may come back to it once, later, only when it fits what the buyer is talking about, and never holds up the next step.
playbook.stage.before_order_form_help: The buyer fills it in the order form. Never asked in chat.
buyer.followup.asked_topic: You asked me to check back today about {topic}.
buyer.followup.asked: You asked me to check back today.

followup.tz: Times are in {tz}. The agent sends it inside your contact hours.
followup.reason.taken_over: a person took over the chat
followup.reason.whatsapp_window_closed: WhatsApp's 24-hour window had closed, so it needs an approved template
followup.reason.send_failed: it could not be sent after 3 tries

buyer.sim.refused.expired: This chat link has expired. Ask {company} for a new link.
buyer.sim.refused.daily_limit: This chat reached today's message limit. Try again tomorrow.
sim.expired_help: This link expired after 14 days without messages. Reset it and send the buyer the new link.
playbook.agent_speaks: How the agent speaks about itself
playbook.agent_speaks_hint: Grammar only. Hebrew, Arabic, French and other languages change words like "assistant" by gender. Neutral avoids gendered forms where the language allows it.
names.agent_hint_after: sell in, never more. A grey name is the automatic version; type over it only to correct it. Automatic versions update when you change the name.
names.trade_hint: Brand names aren't changed automatically: a grey name means buyers see it as written.
names.as_written_notice: No automatic version could be made for {languages} right now, so buyers see the name as written. Type your own version, or save again to try again.
names.none: Your markets sell only in the language the name is typed in, so no other versions are needed.
company.trade_name_hint: Your brand name. Buyers see it as written, unless you add a version for their language.
playbook.questions.budget_hint: The most questions the agent asks before it recommends. 3 suits most sales; use more for complex ones. Only the agent's own questions count.
playbook.fields.too_many_other: {n} questions are needed for the quote, but the agent asks at most {max} before recommending. It will quote the last {extra} on a stated assumption. Raise the number above, or change a question to "Helps the pitch".
playbook.count.title: What counts toward the {max}
playbook.count.sub: Only questions the agent starts count.
playbook.count.ex_agent_1: How do you handle it today?
playbook.count.ex_buyer_1: On paper. Does yours work offline too?
playbook.count.ex_agent_2: Yes, it works offline. How many people will use it?
playbook.count.ex_note: The answer to the buyer's question doesn't count. The new question at the end does.
playbook.count.ex_agent_3: Got it, one office with 12 people. What fits is… Does that sound like what you need?
playbook.count.asap_b: The agent recommends as soon as it can.
playbook.count.asap: The number is a maximum, not a target.
playbook.count.signal_b: A buying signal drops every remaining question
playbook.count.pace: A buyer who asks for more detail gets it; those answers never use up the budget.
playbook.count.ceiling: Safety limit in the app: after {ceiling} questions the agent always recommends, whatever the setting.
